note: 9 of 13 locally-catchable failing CI steps today were tabsii-platform's rls-test lane, which scripts/verify.sh does not run at all (no rls/postgres/docker reference in it). Mechanism: add a pg-test check to biffo-template's scripts/verify.sh using the same CONVENTION the CI lane selects by (test_*_pg.py), so it is verbatim-correct everywhere: repos without such tests print a loud n/a like every other inapplicable check. Resolve a DSN from BIFFO_TEST_PG_DSN/TABSII_TEST_PG_DSN or probe conventional localhost ports, run pytest on the matched modules, and mirror CI's anti-fail-open assertions (a run reporting skips, or no passes, is a FAILURE not a pass) - because the whole defect class here is a lane that reports green having exercised nothing. When no Postgres is reachable it skips LOUDLY naming what did not run, never silently. Second item after this: make practices-daily.sh surface a FATAL run, since today's outage was caught only because a human happened to run the standup.

label: from rank 3: stop the locally-catchable metric going blind — classify the 12 unclassified steps and make blindness fail loudly
note: 12 of 17 estate failing steps are unclassified, all in tabsii-platform, and they are six perfectly classifiable shapes: 'Apply DDL imports' x5, 'Error-branch coverage' x3, 'Initialise database schema' x2, 'Sync portal to S3' x1, 'ADR numbering guard' x1 (the 13th is rls-test, already matched). This is H4's PRIMARY outcome metric (metrics.md:284) and H4 reviews on 2026-08-05, in two days - a verdict read off an 80% that is really 47% would be wrong. It also qualifies yesterday's 13->4 win: the rls cohort really was fixed (9 steps, real), but a 12-step cohort simultaneously fell out of the denominator, so the improvement is smaller than the headline. Mechanism, two parts. (1) Extend STEP_KINDS in scripts/practices-metrics.mjs with patterns for the deploy-side shapes (ddl import, initialise/init database schema, sync .* to s3 -> catchable:false) and the local-guard shapes (error-branch coverage, adr numbering guard -> catchable:true), each as a NAMED kind not a widened generic, so byKind stays arguable. (2) The structural half: unclassified is currently reported-and-ignored, which is the estate's fail-open/reported-zero class again - a metric cannot silently lose 70% of its denominator. Add an estate audit (the practices-daily audit set) that FAILS when unclassified exceeds a threshold share of failingSteps, so the next unseen step name is loud on the day it appears rather than found by a human eyeballing byKind. Watch both fail first against today's snapshot before fixing.

label: make the daily estate-audit harness fail-safe: a grep miss in audit_json silently killed 9 of 10 audits, the dashboard, the snapshot push and today's standup
note: practices-daily.sh runs under 'set -euo pipefail'. audit_json extracts its summary with _summary=$(printf '%s' "$_clean" | grep -E "$3" | tail -1 | sed ...). With pipefail a grep MISS makes that whole pipeline exit 1, the assignment carries the status, and set -e kills the script mid-JSON - so the ${_summary:-no summary line} fallback on the very next line is unreachable dead code. Reproduced exactly: the block dies after audit #1 and leaves a truncated estate-audits.json ending in a comma, byte-for-byte the shape of today's 129-byte file. The script's own comments argue at length that 'a failing audit must REPORT, not abort ... fail-open's mirror image' and guard the audit COMMAND's exit code - but the summary extraction is equally lethal and was missed. Blast radius today, all verified: only 'coverage' ran of 10 audits; no 'estate audits ->', 'page at file://', 'pushed snapshot' or DONE marker; the bookmarked dashboard still reads 'collected 2026-08-03 03:40 UTC'; 2026-08-04.json is untracked and unpushed; and practices-standup.mjs threw SyntaxError on the truncated file, blocking this standup until repaired by hand. Yesterday's newly-added classification audit was silenced on its first morning. Mechanism, three parts. (1) Make the summary extraction non-fatal so the existing fallback actually runs, and on a no-match preserve a snippet of the audit's real output - today's root cause is undiagnosable because _out is discarded unless it matches, so I cannot say WHY hook-audit's '^[0-9]+ working trees' line was absent at 03:41. (2) Write the block to a temp file and mv into place only on success; on harness failure emit WELL-FORMED JSON recording the failure, so downstream never sees truncated garbage nor a silently stale file. (3) practices-standup.mjs currently does existsSync ? JSON.parse : [] - it crashes on a malformed file and, worse, silently ranks with zero audit findings when absent, which is how today's ranking lost every audit-derived finding with no warning. Make unreadable/absent audits a loud warning, not []. Plus a guard test that a no-match audit leaves valid JSON and a live run. No --metric: the audit harness lives outside the snapshot and no collected path captures it, so a metric here would be invented. Tomorrow's observable instead: estate-audits.json contains 10 audit objects and the standup prints audit-derived findings.

label: batch shared-file distribution: nothing schedules shared-sync, so it is run by hand after each template merge
note: Verified: no workflow anywhere references shared-sync.sh - it is entirely manual, run reactively after template merges. Yesterday 19 commits touched shared files (05:24-22:13) and produced ~6.8 rounds x 12 repos = 81 merges, of which 69 are avoidable. That is 100% of the estate's avoidable merges (windows.1.amplification.top has exactly one entry, and its avoidableMerges equals the estate total of 69), so this metric is a pure measure of this one mechanism. A settle-window alone CANNOT fix it: yesterday's changes are spread across 17 hours and are already hand-batched at ~2.7 changes per round, so debouncing bursts leaves ~7 rounds standing. Only a scheduled round collapses 7 to 1, taking 81 merges to ~12-14. Mechanism: (1) add a cron-installable scheduled round, following the same pattern practices-daily.sh already establishes (own log, own invocation-source line, documented crontab line in the header) - shared-sync already requires a local estate checkout via --estate, so the workstation is the right host, not CI; (2) make the ad-hoc path the explicit exception rather than the default - an invocation that would open PRs warns with the pending-change count and the next scheduled round, and requires --now to proceed, because 'people will just stop running it manually' is behavioural and this codebase's own thesis is that documented is not prevented. Honest tradeoff, stated rather than hidden: worst-case distribution latency rises to 24h, which --now exists to escape. Note the current state is already worse on latency - the claim-collision pre-push gate landed at 21:35 and is in ZERO satellites eight hours later, because reactive distribution depends on someone remembering. Tomorrow's check: avoidableMerges 69 -> materially lower, and the drift audit should not be red for a full day.
